candidates.change_summary: Change the block recorded from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2, so lockInGuess returns a different value.
Change the recorded guess from the provided hash parameter to a constant, altering lockInGuess's effect on state.
Change the value requirement from 1 ether to 2 ether, which prevents calls with 1 ether from succeeding, thus changing behavior.
Remove the value requirement, allowing free calls to lockInGuess, which changes the externally observable state after the call.
Replace the duplicate-guess require with a tautology so a second lockInGuess call no longer reverts.
Change the required payment from 1 ether to 0 ether so lockInGuess succeeds with no value sent.
Store the block field as 1 less than the intended target so the recorded height is wrong.
Store the block field as 1 greater than the intended target so the recorded height is wrong.
Delete the first require in lockInGuess, allowing a sender to overwrite a non-zero block entry.
Delete the second require in lockInGuess, allowing calls with less than 1 ether.
Assign block.number instead of block.number + 1, changing the recorded guess block by one.
Assign hash to block instead of guess, swapping which field stores the commitment.
Replace the blockhash input from guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number, changing the answer derivation.
Replace the blockhash input from guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number - 1, altering the answer.
Change the equality check from == to !=, inverting the payout condition.
Remove the transfer, so settle never pays out.
Change transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, changing payout value.
Delete the line that resets guesses[msg.sender].block to 0, so settle can be called multiple times.
Remove the second require, allowing settle to be called before the guessed block passes.
Change the block-number guard from strictly greater than to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settle in the same block as the recorded lock block.
Change the guess-answer comparison to a strict inequality, so a correct guess no longer receives the payout.
Delete the second require so settle no longer requires the current block to exceed the lock block.
Delete the first require so settle can be called even when the caller has no recorded guess.
Weaken the settle timing guard from block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block.
Delete the first require in settle, allowing settlement when no guess was locked in.
Delete the timing require in settle, allowing settlement in the lock-in block itself.
Change the answer hash to use block.number instead of the stored guess block.
Move the guesses[msg.sender].block = 0 state update from before the external transfer call to after it.
Change the answer hash to hash the guess block without including its blockhash.
Replace the require(block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block) with an always-true condition so settle no longer reverts for guesses locked in the current or future block.
Change the answer hash to use the current block's hash instead of the guessed block's hash, altering whether a settled guess can win.
Clear the user's guess block before computing the answer, so a subsequent settle call can pass the nonzero guard check but blockhash(0) is used.
Invert the win condition so the payout occurs when the guess does not match the answer.
